# Per-project idle-workbench and stale pipeline-run reports in the web console

## Description

This epic delivers idle resource reporting in the RHOAI web console: a per-project view showing which workbenches are idle and which pipeline runs are stale, so cluster administrators can see reclaimable capacity in one place. Both reports are read-only views over data that already exists in the platform — the notebook controller's per-workbench last-activity tracking and Kubeflow Pipelines' run completion metadata — with no changes to those backends. Administrators can export either report as CSV for offline analysis.

## Scope

- Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console, showing for each workbench its last activity (from the notebook controller's activity tracking), its owner, and its reserved resources.
- Stale pipeline-run report in the web console, showing completed pipeline runs older than a configurable age threshold, together with their retained artifacts, sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Configurable age threshold for the stale pipeline-run report.
- CSV export of either report, producing the same rows and columns as displayed in the console.
- Read-only reporting only: automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources and cost/chargeback calculations are out of scope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing last-activity dates, when an administrator opens the idle-workbench report for that project, then the report lists each workbench with its last activity, owner, and reserved resources, and the values match the notebook controller's activity tracking for those workbenches.
- Given a project with completed pipeline runs of differing ages, when an administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report, then the report lists exactly the completed runs older than the configured age threshold together with their retained artifacts, and the listing matches Kubeflow Pipelines run completion metadata.
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when the age threshold is changed, then the report reflects the new threshold without redeployment or code change.
- Given either report, when an administrator exports it as CSV, then the exported file contains the same rows and columns as the on-screen report.
- Given a user without administrative access to a project, then the reports do not expose data the user is not entitled to see.
- The reports render for projects with no idle workbenches and no stale runs (empty states), and remain correct when workbench or run data changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- HLR-3 (P2): CSV export of either report.

# Documentation for idle resource reports and safe reclamation steps

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation explaining the new idle resource reports in the RHOAI web console: what each report shows, where the data comes from, how to configure the stale-run age threshold, and how administrators can safely reclaim capacity based on the reports. The documentation describes the reports as implemented in the console.

## Scope

- New documentation topic(s) covering the per-project idle-workbench report: the columns it shows (last activity, owner, reserved resources), its data source, and how to read it.
- New documentation topic(s) covering the stale pipeline-run report: the configurable age threshold, retained artifacts, and its data source.
- Guidance for administrators on safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, including the boundaries of what the platform does automatically (no automated reclamation — reclamation is a manual administrator action).
- Documentation of CSV export of the reports.
- Coverage of the empty-state and role-visibility behavior of the reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports, their data sources, the configurable age threshold, and CSV export, at a level of detail sufficient for a cluster administrator to use the reports without additional support.
- Published documentation includes safe reclamation steps for idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, consistent with the strategy's out-of-scope boundary (no automated reclamation or deletion, no cost/chargeback calculations).
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports and accurately reflects the delivered behavior, fields, and configuration.
- The documentation covers administrator-facing visibility rules for the reports.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps.
